name: Vulshok
description: Red-aligned human mountain barbarians and sorcerers of the Oxidda Chain on Mirrodin, preeminent blacksmiths.

description_citations.text: "Vulshok". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Koth's planeswalker spark ignites as the tribes of his people fall into open war over corrupted ore.
timeline.quote: His planeswalker spark ignited when the tribes of his once peaceful people fell into open war for the first time in generations.

citation.text: "Koth of the Hammer", section "Ascension". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Koth purifies the ore, restoring the metal and slowing the tribal skirmishes.
timeline.quote: Koth believed he could use his ability to purify the ore, and with Koth's help, the solidity of the metal was restored and the skirmishes between tribes slowed.

citation.text: "Koth of the Hammer", section "Ascension". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Phyrexian corruption upsets the balance of the six forge tribes, causing civil war.
timeline.quote: Civil war broke up once more among the barbarians

citation.text: "Vulshok", section "Tribes of the Vulshok". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Koth restores the Vulshok's fragile peace.
timeline.quote: only the act of the new Vulshok leader, Koth could restore their fragile peace.

citation.text: "Vulshok", section "Tribes of the Vulshok". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: The Phyrexian destruction of Mirran culture leaves the Vulshok functionally extinct.
timeline.quote: The Vulshok were rendered functionally extinct from the Phyrexian destruction of Mirran culture
